source.text: שִׁ֗יר הַֽמַּ֫עֲל֥וֹתאֶל־יְ֭הוָה בַּצָּרָ֣תָה לִּ֑י קָ֝רָ֗אתִי וַֽיַּעֲנֵֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: The song of the ascents. To YHWH in the distress to me I called, and he answered me.

en.L: A song of ascents. To {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in my distress I called, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answered me.
en.B: A song of ascents. When I was in trouble I cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave me an answer.
en.R: A song for the journey up to Jerusalem. When I was in trouble, I called to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answered me.

fr.L: Cantique des montées. Vers {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, dans ma détresse, j’ai crié, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} m’a répondu.
fr.B: Cantique des montées. Quand j’étais dans la détresse, j’ai crié vers {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} m’a donné une réponse.
fr.R: Chant pour la montée vers Jérusalem. Quand j’étais en difficulté, j’ai appelé {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} m’a répondu.

sw.L: Wimbo wa kupanda. Kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} katika dhiki yangu nililia, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} akanijibu.
sw.B: Wimbo wa kupanda. Nilipokuwa katika taabu nilimlilia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} akanijibu.
sw.R: Wimbo wa safari ya kupanda kwenda Yerusalemu. Nilipokuwa na shida, nilimwita {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Naye akanijibu.

es.L: Cántico de las subidas. {{divine_name:Al SEÑOR|A Yahvé}} en mi angustia clamé, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} me respondió.
es.B: Cántico de las subidas. Cuando estaba en apuros clamé {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} me dio respuesta.
es.R: Canto para el viaje de subida a Jerusalén. Cuando estaba en problemas, llamé {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. Y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} me respondió.

vi.L: Bài ca cho những lần đi lên. Tôi đã kêu cầu {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} trong cơn khốn quẫn của tôi, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã đáp lời tôi.
vi.B: Bài ca đi lên. Khi tôi gặp hoạn nạn, tôi kêu cầu {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã đáp lời tôi.
vi.R: Bài ca cho cuộc hành trình lên Giê-ru-sa-lem. Khi tôi gặp khó khăn, tôi đã kêu lên cùng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã trả lời tôi.

ko.L: 올라감을 위한 노래. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 내 고난 중에 내가 부르짖었고, 그분께서 내게 응답하셨다.
ko.B: 올라가며 부르는 노래. 내가 고난을 당할 때 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 부르짖었더니, 그분께서 내게 응답해 주셨다.
ko.R: 예루살렘으로 올라가며 부르는 노래. 내가 어려움을 겪을 때 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 불렀다. 그러자 그분께서 내게 대답하셨다.

pt.L: Cântico dos degraus. {{divine_name:Ao SENHOR|A Javé}}, na minha angústia, clamei, e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} me respondeu.
pt.B: Cântico das subidas. Quando eu estava em apuros, clamei {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}, e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} me deu resposta.
pt.R: Canção para a subida a Jerusalém. Quando eu estava em dificuldade, pedi ajuda {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}. E {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} me respondeu.

am.L: የመውጣት መዝሙር። ወደ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} በጭንቀቴ ጠራሁ፤ እርሱም መለሰልኝ።
am.B: የመውጣት መዝሙር። በተቸገርኩ ጊዜ ወደ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ጮኽኩ፤ እርሱም መልስ ሰጠኝ።
am.R: የመውጣት መዝሙር፤ ወደ ኢየሩሳሌም ሲወጡ የሚዘመር። በተቸገርኩ ጊዜ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔርን|ያህዌን}} ጠራሁ። እርሱም መለሰልኝ።

hi.L: चढ़ाई का गीत। {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} को, अपने संकट में, मैंने पुकारा, और उन्होंने मुझे उत्तर दिया।
hi.B: चढ़ाई का गीत। जब मैं संकट में था, तब मैंने {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} की दुहाई दी, और उन्होंने मुझे उत्तर दिया।
hi.R: यरूशलेम की ओर जाने की यात्रा का गीत। जब मैं मुसीबत में था, तब मैंने {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} को पुकारा। और उन्होंने मुझे जवाब दिया।

ru.L: Песнь восхождения. К {{divine_name:ГОСПОДУ|Яхве}} в моей беде я воззвал, и {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} ответил мне.
ru.B: Песнь восхождения. Когда я был в беде, я воззвал к {{divine_name:ГОСПОДУ|Яхве}}, и {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} дал мне ответ.
ru.R: Песня для пути в Иерусалим. Когда мне было трудно, я позвал {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Яхве}}. И {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} ответил мне.

uk.L: Пісня сходжень. До {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Ягве}} в моїй скруті я кликав, і {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} відповів мені.
uk.B: Пісня сходжень. Коли я був у біді, я закликав до {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Ягве}}, і {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} дав мені відповідь.
uk.R: Пісня для подорожі вгору до Єрусалима. Коли я був у біді, я покликав {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Ягве}}. І {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} відповів мені.

decisions.choice: The title shares verse 1
decisions.reason: This psalm's title is short and the Hebrew counts it together with the first line as verse 1, so here the verse numbers are the same as in Bibles that print the title without a number. This is so in all fifteen Songs of Ascents (Psalms 120-134).

decisions.choice: a song of ascents: probably a pilgrim song
alternatives: a song for the temple steps
a song in rising steps of verse
a song of the return from exile
decisions.reason: Each of the fifteen psalms 120-134 carries this title. "Ascents" (ma'alot) means goings up. They were probably sung by pilgrims going up to Jerusalem for the festivals, as 122:1-4 describes (Exodus 23:17; Deuteronomy 16:16). The same word is used of the return from exile in Ezra 7:9, and of steps; other explanations have therefore been given, and the exact sense is not certain.

decisions.choice: past tense: he answered me before
alternatives: present: I call and he answers
decisions.reason: The verbs are in the form usually used for past events. The psalmist remembers that the LORD answered in an earlier trouble, and on that ground prays again in verse 2. Some read the verbs as describing what always happens ("I call, and he answers").

decisions.choice: A song for the journey up to Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Readable says what the title most likely means (see the meaning decision on "ascents"); Literal and Balanced keep the title as it stands.

decisions.choice: "Cantique des montées" (Literal, Balanced); "Chant pour la montée vers Jérusalem" (Readable), for the title of Psalms 120-134
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the song of the ascents". Literal and Balanced keep its words, as the terms note sets for the fifteen Songs of Ascents; Readable says what the title probably means, a song for pilgrims going up to Jerusalem, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "le SEIGNEUR" for the divine name, with "Yahvé" under the reader setting; the speaker prays with "tu"
decisions.reason: The French default writes the name as "le SEIGNEUR" in capitals, like the English "the LORD"; "l'Éternel", the Segond tradition, is the form a reviewer may prefer. In these psalms the speaker addresses God with "tu", the ordinary French of prayer.

decisions.choice: "Wimbo wa kupanda" (L, B); "Wimbo wa safari ya kupanda kwenda Yerusalemu" (R), in every title of Psalms 120-134
decisions.reason: The title says only "a song of the ascents". Literal and Balanced keep that word, "kupanda" (going up); Readable says where the pilgrims went up to, as the English Readable does, since these were probably songs for the road up to Jerusalem (see the meaning decision).

decisions.choice: BWANA in capitals, with Yahwe as the alternative; free pronouns for God such as "naye" carry the deity_pronoun setting
decisions.reason: As in the rest of the Swahili Old Testament. Swahili marks most pronouns inside the verb ("akanijibu", he answered me), where a capital is impossible, so only free pronouns and possessives for God carry the setting.

decisions.choice: "Cántico de las subidas" (L, B); "Canto para el viaje de subida a Jerusalén" (R)
decisions.reason: The title of Psalms 120-134 says only "song of the ascents" (goings up). Literal and Balanced keep the title's own words; Readable explains it, as the English Readable does, as a song for going up to Jerusalem. The same wording is used in all fifteen titles.

decisions.choice: "Bài ca cho những lần đi lên" (L); "Bài ca đi lên" (B); "Bài ca cho cuộc hành trình lên Giê-ru-sa-lem" (R), as the published Psalm 121:1
decisions.reason: The title says only "ascents"; it is probably a pilgrim song for going up to Jerusalem (see the meaning decision). Literal and Balanced keep the title's own word and Readable explains it, as in Psalm 121, and the same titles stand through Psalms 120-134.

decisions.choice: "올라감을 위한 노래" (L), "올라가며 부르는 노래" (B), "예루살렘으로 올라가며 부르는 노래" (R), the wording of the published Psalm 121:1, through Psalms 120-134
decisions.reason: The fifteen Songs of Ascents share one title, so Korean keeps one wording for it at each level. Balanced says what the title most likely means, a song sung on the way up (meaning decision), without naming the temple, which the Hebrew does not; Readable names Jerusalem as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: The singer speaks about the LORD in the plain written style with the honorific (께서, -시-) and calls himself "나"; YHWH is {{divine_name:주|야훼}} with the particle outside the span; no deity_pronoun spans
decisions.reason: Style guide section 7a: speech about God in the plain style, speech to God in 합쇼체 with 저 (from verse 2). Hangul has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change; respect is carried by 그분, 께서 and -시-. This holds for Psalms 120-150.

decisions.choice: Cântico dos degraus (L); Cântico das subidas (B); Canção para a subida a Jerusalém (R)
decisions.reason: For all fifteen Songs of Ascents (120-134): the title is set here and repeated word for word in each, with "De Davi" or "De Salomão" added where the Hebrew has it. Literal keeps the traditional Portuguese name "Cântico dos degraus", by which Brazilian readers know these psalms. Balanced says what the Hebrew ma'alot means, "subidas" (goings up), and keeps the title as it stands, as the English Balanced does; "peregrinação" would already be an interpretation (m2). Readable says what the title most likely means, as the English Readable does (r-en-1). "Cântico" is the book's word for shir (see 3:1); Readable says "Canção".

decisions.choice: A song of ascents as "የመውጣት መዝሙር" at every level, as in all the Songs of Ascents (Psalms 120-134); Readable adds "ወደ ኢየሩሳሌም ሲወጡ የሚዘመር" (sung as they go up to Jerusalem)
alternatives: only the explanation at Readable, as the English
decisions.reason: The terms list's heading for these psalms. Readable keeps the title so the fifteen psalms are still seen as one group, and adds what it most likely means (meaning decision m2), as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in the Amharic of Psalm 120.
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the setting that capitalises pronouns for God has nothing to change in Amharic; pronouns and verb forms for God are written plainly.

decisions.choice: "{{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}}" for the name YHWH; "प्रभु" alone for the title Adonai; no deity_pronoun spans
decisions.reason: Hindi says "प्रभु" both for the name YHWH and for the title Adonai ("Lord"). Where it stands for the name, the text carries the divine_name setting, whose alternative "याहवे" gives the name itself, so with the setting on a reader can tell the two apart through Psalms 120-136. Devanagari has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change: God spoken of takes the honorific plural ("उन्होंने"), and the psalmist speaks to God with the devotional "तू".

decisions.choice: "चढ़ाई का गीत" (L, B); "यरूशलेम की ओर जाने की यात्रा का गीत" (R)
decisions.reason: This title heads each of Psalms 120-134 and has one form per level in Hindi, as the poetry note's table of titles has it. Literal and Balanced keep the Hebrew's "song of the ascents"; Readable says what it most likely means, a song for pilgrims going up to Jerusalem (meaning m2), as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: Песнь восхождения (L, B); Песня для пути в Иерусалим (R)
decisions.reason: Shir hamma'alot: as the poetry note settles, Literal and Balanced keep the title's words, "Песнь восхождения", and Readable says what it most likely means (m2), "Песня для пути в Иерусалим", as the English level does. One form per level through Psalms 120-134.

decisions.choice: "Пісня сходжень" (L, B), "Пісня для подорожі вгору до Єрусалима" (R) for the titles of Psalms 120-134
decisions.reason: The heading probably names the pilgrims' songs on the way up to Jerusalem; Literal and Balanced keep the word for going up, and Readable says where they went, as its English does.

source.text: יְֽהוָ֗ה הַצִּ֣ילָה נַ֭פְשִׁי מִשְּׂפַת־שֶׁ֑קֶר מִלָּשׁ֥וֹן רְמִיָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: YHWH, deliver my soul from a lip of falsehood, from a tongue of deceit.

en.L: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, deliver my soul from a lip of falsehood, from a tongue of deceit.
en.B: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, rescue me from people whose lips tell lies, whose tongues deceive.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, save me from liars and from people who trick others.

fr.L: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, délivre mon âme de la lèvre de mensonge, de la langue de tromperie.
fr.B: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, arrache-moi aux gens dont les lèvres mentent, dont la langue trompe.
fr.R: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, sauve-moi des menteurs et des gens qui trompent les autres.

sw.L: Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, uiokoe nafsi yangu na mdomo wa uongo, na ulimi wa hila.
sw.B: Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, uniokoe na watu ambao midomo yao husema uongo, ambao ndimi zao hudanganya.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, niokoe kutoka kwa waongo na kwa watu wanaowadanganya wengine.

es.L: {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, libra mi alma del labio de mentira, de la lengua de engaño.
es.B: {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, rescátame de la gente cuyos labios dicen mentiras, cuyas lenguas engañan.
es.R: {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, sálvame de los mentirosos y de la gente que engaña a los demás.

vi.L: Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, xin giải cứu linh hồn tôi khỏi môi giả dối, khỏi lưỡi lừa gạt.
vi.B: Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, xin cứu tôi khỏi những kẻ có môi nói dối, có lưỡi lừa gạt.
vi.R: Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, xin cứu tôi khỏi những kẻ nói dối và những kẻ lừa gạt người khác.

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 거짓의 입술에서, 속임의 혀에서 제 영혼을 건져 주십시오.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 거짓말하는 입술과 속이는 혀를 가진 사람들에게서 저를 건져 주십시오.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 거짓말쟁이들과 남을 속이는 사람들에게서 저를 구해 주십시오.

pt.L: {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, livra a minha alma do lábio de falsidade, da língua de engano.
pt.B: {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, livra-me das pessoas que mentem com os lábios e enganam com a língua.
pt.R: {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, salva-me dos mentirosos e das pessoas que enganam os outros.

am.L: {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ሆይ፣ ነፍሴን ከሐሰተኛ ከንፈር፣ ከተንኰለኛ ምላስ አድናት።
am.B: {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ሆይ፣ ከንፈሮቻቸው ከሚዋሹ፣ ምላሶቻቸውም ከሚያታልሉ ሰዎች አድነኝ።
am.R: {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ሆይ፣ ከውሸታሞችና ሌሎችን ከሚያታልሉ ሰዎች አድነኝ።

hi.L: हे {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}}, मेरे प्राण को झूठ के होंठ से, छल की जीभ से छुड़ा।
hi.B: हे {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}}, मुझे उन लोगों से छुड़ा जिनके होंठ झूठ बोलते हैं, जिनकी जीभ छल करती है।
hi.R: हे {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}}, मुझे झूठे लोगों से और दूसरों को धोखा देनेवालों से बचा।

ru.L: {{divine_name:ГОСПОДИ|Яхве}}, избавь душу мою от губ лжи, от языка обмана.
ru.B: {{divine_name:ГОСПОДИ|Яхве}}, избавь меня от людей, чьи губы говорят ложь, чьи языки обманывают.
ru.R: {{divine_name:ГОСПОДИ|Яхве}}, спаси меня от лжецов и от тех, кто обманывает других.

uk.L: {{divine_name:ГОСПОДИ|Ягве}}, визволи мою душу від уст неправди, від язика підступу.
uk.B: {{divine_name:ГОСПОДИ|Ягве}}, урятуй мене від людей, чиї уста брешуть, чиї язики обманюють.
uk.R: {{divine_name:ГОСПОДИ|Ягве}}, урятуй мене від брехунів і від людей, які обдурюють інших.

decisions.choice: lip, tongue: the people who speak
decisions.reason: "A lip of falsehood" and "a tongue of deceit" stand for the people who speak that way. The psalm does not say what the lies were; verses 6-7 set them against the psalmist's wish for peace.

decisions.choice: deceit: treachery
decisions.reason: The word (remiyyah) means deceit or treachery, words meant to mislead (52:6; Micah 6:12).

decisions.choice: my soul (L); me (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in Psalms 1-12, nefesh is "soul" at Literal; Balanced and Readable say "me" or "my life", since the word means the whole living person.

decisions.choice: people whose lips tell lies (B); liars (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the people that the lips and tongue stand for (m1).

decisions.choice: "mon âme" at Literal; "moi" at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: Nefesh is "âme" at Literal, as the terms note sets; here it stands for the whole person, so Balanced and Readable say "me", as the English does.

decisions.choice: "nafsi yangu" (my soul) at Literal; "mimi" (me) at Balanced and Readable, through Psalms 120-150
decisions.reason: The Hebrew nefesh is the whole living person. Literal keeps the word "nafsi"; Balanced and Readable say the person, as the English does. "Roho" would suggest the spirit apart from the body.

decisions.choice: mi alma (L); me (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew nefesh is the living self. Literal keeps "alma", as the English Literal keeps "soul"; Balanced and Readable say simply "me", as the English does.

decisions.choice: "Lạy CHÚA" and "xin" when the psalmist calls on God and asks, unbracketed at Literal
alternatives: the bare name and a bare imperative
decisions.reason: Vietnamese calls on God with "Lạy" and asks with "xin"; both belong to the grammar of prayer, as in the published Psalm 139, so Literal does not bracket them.

decisions.choice: Speaking to God the singer turns to 합쇼체 and calls himself "저/제"; God is called "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}여" and, where a "you" is needed, addressed by the title "주님"
decisions.reason: Style guide section 7a (speech levels in prayer), as the published Psalms 23 and 139. Korean addresses a superior by title, not by a pronoun. The vocative "여" stands outside the span and fits both forms.

decisions.choice: "제 영혼" (L); "저" (B, R) for nefesh
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the word the terms note gives for nefesh; Balanced and Readable say the person, as the English "me" does.
As the poetry note settles for nefesh: "प्राण" at Literal, and the person himself at Balanced and Readable, as the English does. "आत्मा" is kept for the spirit.

decisions.choice: душу мою (L); меня (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in the earlier psalms, nefesh is душа at Literal; Balanced and Readable say "me", "I" or "life" as the English level does, since the word means the whole living person.

source.text: מַה־יִּתֵּ֣ן לְ֭ךָ וּמַה־יֹּסִ֥יף לָ֗ךְ לָשׁ֥וֹן רְמִיָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: What will he give to you, and what will he add to you, tongue of deceit?

en.L: What will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} give to you, and what will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} add to you, [you] tongue of deceit?
en.B: You deceitful tongue, what will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} give you, and what more will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} heap on you?
en.R: You liars, what will God give you in return? What more will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} add?

fr.L: Que te donnera-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}}, et que t’ajoutera-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}}, langue de tromperie ?
fr.B: Langue trompeuse, que te donnera-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}}, et que fera-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} pleuvoir encore sur toi ?
fr.R: Menteurs, que va-t-il vous arriver de la part de Dieu ? Que va-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} encore ajouter ?

sw.L: Atakupa nini, na atakuongezea nini, [wewe] ulimi wa hila?
sw.B: Ewe ulimi wa udanganyifu, atakupa nini, na atakuzidishia nini zaidi?
sw.R: Ninyi waongo, Mungu atawapa nini kama malipo? Ataongeza nini zaidi?

es.L: ¿Qué te dará {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, y qué más te añadirá, [tú,] lengua de engaño?
es.B: Lengua engañosa, ¿qué te dará {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, y qué más amontonará sobre ti?
es.R: Mentirosos, ¿qué {{plural_you:les|os}} dará Dios a cambio? ¿Qué más {{plural_you:les|os}} añadirá?

vi.L: Ngài sẽ ban cho ngươi điều gì, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ thêm cho ngươi điều gì nữa, hỡi lưỡi lừa gạt kia?
vi.B: Hỡi lưỡi lừa gạt kia, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ ban cho ngươi điều gì, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ giáng thêm trên ngươi điều gì nữa?
vi.R: Hỡi những kẻ nói dối, Đức Chúa Trời sẽ báo trả các ngươi điều gì? Ngài sẽ thêm cho các ngươi điều gì nữa?

ko.L: 그분께서 너에게 무엇을 주시고, 너에게 무엇을 더하시겠느냐, 속임의 혀야?
ko.B: 속이는 혀야, 그분께서 너에게 무엇을 주시겠느냐? 무엇을 더 얹어 주시겠느냐?
ko.R: 거짓말쟁이들아, 하나님께서 너희에게 무엇으로 갚으시겠느냐? 무엇을 더 내리시겠느냐?

pt.L: O que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} lhe dará, e o que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} lhe acrescentará, [ó] língua de engano?
pt.B: Língua enganadora, o que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} vai dar a você? E o que mais {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} vai jogar sobre você?
pt.R: Mentirosos, o que Deus vai dar a vocês em troca? O que mais {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} vai acrescentar?

am.L: አንተ ተንኰለኛ ምላስ፣ ምን ይሰጥሃል? ምንስ ይጨምርብሃል?
am.B: አንተ አታላይ ምላስ፣ ምን ይሰጥሃል? ከዚህስ በላይ ምን ይከምርብሃል?
am.R: እናንተ ውሸታሞች፣ እግዚአብሔር ምን ብድራት ይከፍላችኋል? ከዚህስ በላይ ምን ይጨምርባችኋል?

hi.L: वे तुम्हें क्या देंगे, और तुम पर और क्या बढ़ाएँगे, [हे] छल की जीभ?
hi.B: हे छल करनेवाली जीभ, वे तुम्हें क्या देंगे, और तुम पर और क्या लादेंगे?
hi.R: हे झूठे लोगो, परमेश्वर तुम्हें बदले में क्या देंगे? वे और क्या जोड़ेंगे?

ru.L: Что даст тебе {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} и что прибавит тебе {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}}, [ты,] язык обмана?
ru.B: Лживый язык, что {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} даст тебе и что ещё {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} обрушит на тебя?
ru.R: Лжецы, что Бог даст вам в ответ? Что ещё {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} прибавит?

uk.L: Що {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} дасть тобі, і що {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} додасть тобі, [ти], язику підступу?
uk.B: Ти, підступний язику, що {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} дасть тобі і що ще {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} навалить на тебе?
uk.R: Ви, брехуни, що Бог дасть вам у відплату? Що ще {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} додасть?

decisions.choice: give ... add: the words of an oath of punishment
decisions.reason: "May God do so to you and add more" was a way of calling down punishment (1 Samuel 3:17; Ruth 1:17). The question takes up those words: what will God do to the liar, and what more besides? Verse 4 gives the answer.

decisions.choice: he: God
alternatives: impersonal: what shall be given to you
decisions.reason: The verbs have "he" as subject. In the oath formula that "he" is God, so the liar is asked what God will give in return. The verbs may also be impersonal, "what shall be done to you".

decisions.choice: tongue of deceit: spoken to the liar
decisions.reason: The psalmist turns and speaks directly to the "deceitful tongue" of verse 2, that is, to the liar.

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who gives (m2), and speaks to "liars" (m3).

decisions.choice: "Menteurs" with "vous" at Readable, where Literal and Balanced speak to the "langue" with "tu"
decisions.reason: The tongue stands for the liars, as the English Readable says "You liars"; French then needs the plural "vous".

decisions.choice: the liar addressed as "Mentirosos", plural
decisions.reason: The Hebrew speaks to one "tongue of deceit"; the English Readable turns it into "You liars". Spanish Readable follows it with a plural address, so its pronouns carry the plural_you setting ("les" or "os").

decisions.choice: "ngươi" (L, B), "các ngươi" (R) for the liar spoken to
decisions.reason: The psalmist turns on the liar with scorn. "ngươi" is the stern literary word of address to an enemy; "mày" would be coarse and "anh" friendly. Readable speaks to the liars as a group, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: The liar is spoken to in 해라체 ("너", "-느냐"); Readable "거짓말쟁이들아" with "너희"
decisions.reason: The singer turns to address the deceitful tongue (meaning decision); Korean speaks to an opponent in the plain style. Readable names the liars, as the English Readable does, and so speaks to them in the plural.

decisions.choice: lhe, você (L, B); vocês (R)
decisions.reason: The psalmist turns to the liar (m3), a person, so Portuguese uses the forms of "você", as Psalm 52:6 does for the "língua de engano"; "tu" is kept for words to God. Readable speaks to "Mentirosos" in the plural, as the English Readable says "You liars".

decisions.choice: the address "አንተ ተንኰለኛ ምላስ" put first
alternatives: the address at the end, as the Hebrew
decisions.reason: Amharic puts a vocative before the question it belongs to; leaving it after both questions would read as a third, unfinished sentence.

decisions.choice: "तुम" to the deceitful tongue; God as "वे"
decisions.reason: The psalmist turns to the liar (meaning m3). In this translation "तू" is kept for God, so the liar is spoken to with "तुम"; the one who gives and adds is God (m2), spoken of with the honorific plural.

decisions.choice: вам (plural)
decisions.reason: Readable speaks to "liars", as the English level does (m3), so Russian uses вы for the plural; Literal and Balanced keep the single "tongue" addressed with ты.

source.text: חִצֵּ֣י גִבּ֣וֹר שְׁנוּנִ֑ים עִ֝֗ם גַּחֲלֵ֥י רְתָמִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Arrows of a warrior, sharpened, with coals of broom plants.

en.L: Arrows of a warrior, sharpened, with coals of broom [wood]!
en.B: Sharpened arrows from a fighter's bow, and hot coals of broom wood!
en.R: Here is what you will get: a soldier's sharp arrows and red-hot coals that burn a long time.

fr.L: Des flèches de guerrier, aiguisées, avec des braises de genêt !
fr.B: Les flèches aiguisées d’un combattant, et des braises ardentes de genêt !
fr.R: Voici ce que vous recevrez : les flèches pointues d’un soldat et des braises brûlantes qui restent chaudes longtemps.

sw.L: Mishale ya shujaa, iliyonolewa, pamoja na makaa ya [mti wa] mretemu!
sw.B: Mishale mikali ya mpiganaji hodari, na makaa ya moto ya mti wa mretemu!
sw.R: Hiki ndicho mtakachopata: mishale mikali ya askari, na makaa ya moto yanayowaka kwa muda mrefu.

es.L: ¡Flechas de guerrero, afiladas, con brasas de retama!
es.B: ¡Flechas afiladas del arco de un guerrero, y brasas ardientes de leña de retama!
es.R: Esto es lo que van a recibir: las flechas afiladas de un soldado y brasas al rojo vivo que arden mucho tiempo.

vi.L: Những mũi tên của dũng sĩ, đã mài nhọn, cùng với than hồng của [cây] đậu chổi!
vi.B: Những mũi tên nhọn sắc của người chiến binh, và than hồng bằng gỗ cây đậu chổi!
vi.R: Đây là điều các ngươi sẽ nhận: những mũi tên sắc của người lính, và những cục than đỏ rực cháy rất lâu.

ko.L: 용사의 화살들, 날카롭게 간 것들, 로뎀 [나무] 숯불과 함께!
ko.B: 용사의 활에서 나온 날카로운 화살과 로뎀나무의 뜨거운 숯불이다!
ko.R: 너희가 받을 것은 이것이다. 군인의 날카로운 화살과, 오래도록 타는 시뻘건 숯불이다.

pt.L: Flechas de guerreiro, afiadas, com brasas de giesta!
pt.B: Flechas afiadas do arco de um combatente, e brasas ardentes de giesta!
pt.R: Isto é o que vocês vão receber: as flechas afiadas de um soldado e brasas bem quentes, que queimam por muito tempo.

am.L: የኃያል ሰው የተሳሉ ፍላጻዎች፣ ከክትክታ [እንጨት] ፍም ጋር!
am.B: ከተዋጊ ቀስት የሚወረወሩ የተሳሉ ፍላጻዎችና የጋለ የክትክታ እንጨት ፍም!
am.R: የምታገኙት ይህ ነው፦ የወታደር ስለታም ፍላጻዎችና ለረጅም ጊዜ የሚነድ የጋለ ፍም።

hi.L: योद्धा के तीर, पैने किए हुए, झाऊ [की लकड़ी] के अंगारों के साथ!
hi.B: किसी योद्धा के पैने तीर, और झाऊ की लकड़ी के दहकते अंगारे!
hi.R: तुम्हें यह मिलेगा: सैनिक के तेज़ तीर और ऐसे दहकते अंगारे जो देर तक जलते रहते हैं।

ru.L: Стрелы воина заострённые, с углями ракитника!
ru.B: Острые стрелы из лука бойца и раскалённые угли ракитника!
ru.R: Вот что вы получите: острые стрелы воина и раскалённые угли, которые горят долго.

uk.L: Стріли воїна, нагострені, з жаром ратамового [дерева]!
uk.B: Нагострені стріли з лука воїна і гаряче вугілля з ратаму!
uk.R: Ось що ви отримаєте: гострі стріли воїна і розпечене вугілля, яке довго горить.

decisions.choice: the answer to verse 3: the punishment
alternatives: a picture of the deceitful tongue itself
decisions.reason: The verse answers the question of verse 3: the liar will receive sharp arrows and burning coals, a fitting reward for a tongue that wounds like arrows and burns like fire (57:5; 64:4; James 3:6). Others read it as a description of the tongue itself.

decisions.choice: broom: a desert shrub that burns hot and long
decisions.reason: The broom (rotem) is a shrub of the desert (1 Kings 19:4; Job 30:4). Its wood makes charcoal that burns very hot and keeps its heat a long time.

decisions.choice: Here is what you will get
decisions.reason: Readable makes the link to the question of verse 3 explicit (m1), and says what broom coals are like (m2).

decisions.choice: "genêt" for the broom shrub
decisions.reason: The rotem is the white broom of the desert, "genêt" in French; its charcoal burns hot and long, which Readable explains instead of naming the plant.

decisions.choice: "mretemu" for the broom bush
decisions.reason: "Mretemu" is the Swahili name of the broom bush of the desert, whose wood makes hot, long-lasting coals; Readable says what the coals do instead of naming the plant, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "cây đậu chổi" for the broom shrub (L, B); Readable describes the coals
decisions.reason: The plant is a desert shrub whose wood makes coals that burn hot and long (see the meaning decision). "đậu chổi" names the broom plant plainly; Readable says only what matters, that the coals burn a long time, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "로뎀 [나무]" (L), "로뎀나무" (B) for the broom shrub; Readable describes its coals
decisions.reason: "로뎀나무" is the name Korean readers know for this desert shrub (1 Kings 19:4); Readable says what matters here, coals that burn a long time, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: giesta
decisions.reason: The desert shrub (m2) is "giesta", as in 1 Kings 19:4 and Job 30:4 in Portuguese; "zimbro" is a juniper, a different plant. Readable says what its coals are like instead of naming it, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: broom as "ክትክታ" (L, B), as 1 Kings 19:4-5
decisions.reason: The desert shrub whose wood burns hot and long (meaning decision m2); the Amharic of 1 Kings 19 names Elijah's broom tree "ክትክታ", and the psalm keeps that word. Readable says only what the coals do, as the English.

decisions.choice: "झाऊ"
decisions.reason: The desert broom shrub (meaning m2) is "झाऊ", as for Elijah's broom tree in 1 Kings 19:4 in this translation. Readable says what its coals are like instead, as the English does.

decisions.choice: угли ракитника
decisions.reason: The rotem is the desert broom (m2); ракитник is the word this translation uses for Elijah's broom tree (1 Kings 19:4). The Synodal's можжевельник (juniper) names another plant.

source.text: אֽוֹיָה־לִ֭י כִּי־גַ֣רְתִּי מֶ֑שֶׁךְ שָׁ֝כַ֗נְתִּי עִֽם־אָהֳלֵ֥י קֵדָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: Woe to me, that I have sojourned [in] Meshech, I have dwelt with [the] tents of Kedar.

en.L: Woe to me, that I sojourn [in] Meshech, [that] I dwell among [the] tents of Kedar!
en.B: How miserable I am, living as a foreigner in Meshech, making my home among the tents of Kedar!
en.R: How terrible it is for me! I am like a stranger living far away in Meshech, or among the tents of Kedar.

fr.L: Malheur à moi, car je séjourne [à] Méshek, [car] je demeure parmi les tentes de Qédar !
fr.B: Quel malheur pour moi de vivre en étranger à Méshek, d’habiter parmi les tentes de Qédar !
fr.R: Comme c’est dur pour moi ! Je suis comme un étranger qui vit loin, à Méshek, ou parmi les tentes de Qédar.

sw.L: Ole wangu, kwa kuwa ninakaa kama mgeni [katika] Mesheki, [kwamba] ninaishi kati ya mahema ya Kedari!
sw.B: Ni taabu kwangu, kuishi kama mgeni huko Mesheki, kufanya makao yangu kati ya mahema ya Kedari!
sw.R: Ni vibaya mno kwangu! Mimi ni kama mgeni anayeishi mbali huko Mesheki, au kati ya mahema ya Kedari.

es.L: ¡Ay de mí, que vivo como extranjero [en] Mesec, [que] habito entre [las] tiendas de Cedar!
es.B: ¡Qué desdichado soy, viviendo como extranjero en Mesec, haciendo mi hogar entre las tiendas de Cedar!
es.R: ¡Qué terrible es para mí! Soy como un extranjero que vive lejos, en Mesec, o entre las tiendas de Cedar.

vi.L: Khốn cho tôi, vì tôi ngụ [ở] Mê-siếc, [vì] tôi ở giữa [các] trại của Kê-đa!
vi.B: Tôi khốn khổ biết bao, phải sống như kẻ lạ ở Mê-siếc, phải ở giữa những trại của Kê-đa!
vi.R: Thật khổ cho tôi! Tôi như một người xa lạ sống tận Mê-siếc, hay giữa những trại của Kê-đa.

ko.L: 내게 화가 있다, 내가 메섹에 나그네로 머물고, 게달의 장막들 가운데 거하니!
ko.B: 아, 비참한 내 신세여! 메섹에서 나그네로 살며 게달의 장막들 사이에 거처를 두다니!
ko.R: 아, 나는 정말 괴롭다! 나는 먼 메섹 땅에 사는 나그네 같고, 게달 사람들의 장막 사이에 사는 사람 같다.

pt.L: Ai de mim, que moro como estrangeiro [em] Meseque, [que] habito entre [as] tendas de Quedar!
pt.B: Como sou infeliz! Vivo como estrangeiro em Meseque e faço a minha casa entre as tendas de Quedar!
pt.R: Como é triste a minha vida! Sou como um estrangeiro que mora longe, em Meseque, ou entre as tendas de Quedar.

am.L: ወዮልኝ፣ በሞሳሕ መጻተኛ ሆኜ የምኖር፣ በቄዳር ድንኳኖች መካከል የምቀመጥ!
am.B: በሞሳሕ እንደ መጻተኛ የምኖር፣ በቄዳር ድንኳኖች መካከል መኖሪያዬን ያደረግኩ እኔ እንዴት ጐስቋላ ነኝ!
am.R: ወዮልኝ! በሩቅ አገር በሞሳሕ ወይም በቄዳር ድንኳኖች መካከል እንደሚኖር እንግዳ ነኝ።

hi.L: हाय मुझ पर, कि मैं मेशेक में परदेशी होकर रहता हूँ, [कि] मैं केदार के तंबुओं के बीच बसता हूँ!
hi.B: मैं कितना दुखी हूँ, कि मेशेक में परदेशी बनकर रहता हूँ, केदार के तंबुओं के बीच अपना घर बनाए हुए हूँ!
hi.R: मेरा कितना बुरा हाल है! मैं ऐसे परदेशी की तरह हूँ जो दूर मेशेक में रहता है, या केदार के तंबुओं के बीच।

ru.L: Горе мне, что я живу пришельцем [в] Мешехе, [что] обитаю у шатров Кедара!
ru.B: Как я несчастен, что живу чужеземцем в Мешехе, что мой дом среди шатров Кедара!
ru.R: Как мне тяжело! Я словно чужой, живущий далеко, в Мешехе, или среди шатров Кедара.

uk.L: Горе мені, що я живу приходьком [у] Мешеху, [що] я мешкаю серед наметів Кедару!
uk.B: Який я нещасний, що живу як чужинець у Мешеху, що мій дім серед наметів Кедару!
uk.R: Як тяжко мені! Я ніби чужинець, що живе далеко в Мешеху або серед наметів Кедару.

decisions.choice: Meshech and Kedar: distant, warlike peoples
decisions.reason: Meshech was a people of the far north, in what is now Turkey (Genesis 10:2; Ezekiel 38:2); Kedar was a tribe of the Arabian desert, known for its archers (Genesis 25:13; Isaiah 21:16-17). The two lie far apart, so the psalmist is probably not living in both: the names are a picture of living among fierce, hostile people.

decisions.choice: sojourn: live as a foreigner
decisions.reason: The verb (gur) means to live somewhere as an outsider without the rights of a citizen.

decisions.choice: I am like a stranger
decisions.reason: Readable shows that the place names are a picture (m1).

decisions.choice: "Méshek" and "Qédar"
decisions.reason: The names are transcribed from the Hebrew with French spelling; Qédar keeps the q of the Hebrew as many French Bibles do. Both are distant peoples, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: "Mê-siếc" and "Kê-đa" for Meshech and Kedar
decisions.reason: The names take the Protestant tradition's transliterations, which Vietnamese Bible readers know.

decisions.choice: Meshech as "ሞሳሕ", Kedar as "ቄዳር"
decisions.reason: The forms of the names in the Amharic of Genesis 10:2, 25:13 and 1 Chronicles 1.

decisions.choice: "मेशेक", "केदार"; "परदेशी होकर रहना"
decisions.reason: The names keep their forms from Genesis 10:2 and 25:13 in this translation. To sojourn is to live as a foreigner (meaning m2): "परदेशी", as the Pentateuch note has it for ger.

decisions.choice: пришельцем (L); чужеземцем (B)
decisions.reason: Gur, to live as a foreigner (m2), takes the Pentateuch note's word for the ger: пришелец at Literal, чужеземец otherwise. Мешех and Кедар keep their forms from Genesis 10 and 25.

source.text: רַ֭בַּת שָֽׁכְנָה־לָּ֣הּ נַפְשִׁ֑י עִ֝֗ם שׂוֹנֵ֥א שָׁלֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: Much has dwelt for itself my soul with [one who] hates peace.

en.L: Long has my soul dwelt with [one who] hates peace.
en.B: For far too long I have had to live beside people who hate peace.
en.R: I have spent too much of my life near people who hate peace.

fr.L: Longtemps mon âme a demeuré pour elle-même avec [celui qui] hait la paix.
fr.B: Depuis bien trop longtemps je dois vivre à côté de gens qui haïssent la paix.
fr.R: J’ai passé trop de temps de ma vie près de gens qui détestent la paix.

sw.L: Muda mrefu nafsi yangu imekaa pamoja na achukiaye amani.
sw.B: Kwa muda mrefu mno nimelazimika kuishi karibu na watu wanaochukia amani.
sw.R: Nimeishi muda mrefu sana karibu na watu wanaochukia amani.

es.L: Mucho tiempo ha habitado mi alma con [el que] odia la paz.
es.B: Durante demasiado tiempo he tenido que vivir junto a gente que odia la paz.
es.R: He pasado gran parte de mi vida cerca de gente que odia la paz.

vi.L: Linh hồn tôi đã ở lâu với [kẻ] ghét sự bình an.
vi.B: Đã quá lâu tôi phải sống bên cạnh những kẻ ghét sự bình an.
vi.R: Tôi đã sống quá lâu gần những người ghét hòa bình.

ko.L: 오랫동안 내 영혼이 평화를 미워하는 [자]와 함께 거하였다.
ko.B: 평화를 미워하는 사람들 곁에서 내가 너무도 오래 살아왔다.
ko.R: 나는 평화를 싫어하는 사람들 가까이에서 너무 오랫동안 살았다.

pt.L: Por muito tempo a minha alma habitou com [quem] odeia a paz.
pt.B: Faz tempo demais que tenho de viver ao lado de gente que odeia a paz.
pt.R: Passei tempo demais da minha vida perto de pessoas que odeiam a paz.

am.L: ነፍሴ ሰላምን ከሚጠላ ጋር ብዙ ተቀመጠች።
am.B: ሰላምን ከሚጠሉ ሰዎች አጠገብ እጅግ ረጅም ጊዜ ኖርኩ።
am.R: ሰላምን በሚጠሉ ሰዎች አጠገብ ብዙ ዕድሜዬን አሳለፍኩ።

hi.L: बहुत समय से मेरा प्राण शान्ति से बैर रखनेवाले के साथ बसा है।
hi.B: बहुत लंबे समय से मुझे ऐसे लोगों के पास रहना पड़ा है जो शान्ति से बैर रखते हैं।
hi.R: मैंने अपनी ज़िंदगी का बहुत बड़ा हिस्सा ऐसे लोगों के पास बिताया है जो शान्ति से नफ़रत करते हैं।

ru.L: Долго жила душа моя с ненавидящим мир.
ru.B: Слишком долго мне пришлось жить рядом с людьми, которые ненавидят мир.
ru.R: Я слишком долго прожил рядом с людьми, которые ненавидят мир.

uk.L: Довго жила моя душа з [тим, хто] ненавидить мир.
uk.B: Надто довго мені довелося жити поруч із людьми, які ненавидять мир.
uk.R: Я прожив надто багато часу поруч із людьми, які ненавидять мир.

decisions.choice: much: too long
decisions.reason: The word (rabbat) means "much" or "for a long time"; here it carries the sense of "far too long". It returns in 123:4 and 129:1-2.

decisions.choice: one who hates peace: a type
decisions.reason: The singular "one who hates" stands for the kind of people around the psalmist; verse 7 calls them "they".

decisions.choice: my soul (L); I (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in Psalms 1-12, nefesh is "soul" at Literal; Balanced and Readable say "me" or "my life", since the word means the whole living person.

decisions.choice: people who hate peace
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the singular type plural (m2), as verse 7 does.

decisions.choice: "hòa bình" (R) for "peace" between people; "sự bình an" (L, B)
decisions.reason: Here peace is good relations between neighbours (see the meaning decision). Readable uses the everyday word for not fighting; Literal and Balanced keep the key term.

decisions.choice: "평화" for shalom between people and over a city (120:6-7; 122; 125:5; 128:6)
decisions.reason: Here the word is the opposite of war (verse 7), so Korean says "평화"; "평안", the word kept for inner peace in John, would miss the contrast.

decisions.choice: душа моя (L); я (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in the earlier psalms, nefesh is душа at Literal; Balanced and Readable say "me", "I" or "life" as the English level does, since the word means the whole living person.

records.literal_gloss: I [am] peace, and when I speak, they [are] for war.

en.L: I [am] peace; but when I speak, they [are] for war.
en.B: I stand for peace, but when I open my mouth, they choose war.
en.R: I want peace. But every time I speak, they want to fight.

fr.L: Moi, [je suis] paix ; mais quand je parle, eux [sont] pour la guerre.
fr.B: Moi, je suis pour la paix, mais dès que j’ouvre la bouche, ils choisissent la guerre.
fr.R: Moi, je veux la paix. Mais chaque fois que je parle, ils veulent se battre.

sw.L: Mimi [ni] amani; lakini ninaposema, wao [ni] kwa ajili ya vita.
sw.B: Mimi ninasimama upande wa amani, lakini ninapofungua kinywa changu, wao wanachagua vita.
sw.R: Mimi ninataka amani. Lakini kila ninaposema, wao wanataka kupigana.

es.L: Yo [soy] paz; pero cuando hablo, ellos [son] para la guerra.
es.B: Yo estoy por la paz, pero cuando abro la boca, ellos escogen la guerra.
es.R: Yo quiero la paz. Pero cada vez que hablo, ellos quieren pelear.

vi.L: Tôi [là] sự bình an; nhưng khi tôi nói, chúng [là] vì chiến tranh.
vi.B: Tôi muốn sự bình an, nhưng hễ tôi mở miệng, chúng lại chọn chiến tranh.
vi.R: Tôi muốn hòa bình. Nhưng mỗi lần tôi nói, chúng lại muốn đánh nhau.

ko.L: 나는 평화[이다]. 그러나 내가 말할 때 그들은 전쟁을 [원한다].
ko.B: 나는 평화의 편에 서 있지만, 내가 입을 열기만 하면 그들은 전쟁을 택한다.
ko.R: 나는 평화를 바란다. 그러나 내가 말할 때마다 그들은 싸우려고 한다.

pt.L: Eu [sou] paz; mas, quando falo, eles [são] pela guerra.
pt.B: Eu sou a favor da paz, mas, quando abro a boca, eles escolhem a guerra.
pt.R: Eu quero paz. Mas, sempre que falo, eles querem lutar.

am.L: እኔ ሰላም [ነኝ]፤ በተናገርኩ ጊዜ ግን እነርሱ ለጦርነት [ናቸው]።
am.B: እኔ ለሰላም እቆማለሁ፤ አፌን በከፈትኩ ቁጥር ግን እነርሱ ጦርነትን ይመርጣሉ።
am.R: እኔ ሰላምን እፈልጋለሁ። በተናገርኩ ቁጥር ግን እነርሱ መዋጋት ይፈልጋሉ።

hi.L: मैं शान्ति [हूँ]; पर जब मैं बोलता हूँ, तो वे युद्ध के लिए [हैं]।
hi.B: मैं शान्ति के पक्ष में हूँ, पर जब मैं मुँह खोलता हूँ, तो वे युद्ध चुनते हैं।
hi.R: मैं शान्ति चाहता हूँ। पर जब भी मैं बोलता हूँ, वे लड़ना चाहते हैं।

ru.L: Я — мир; но когда я говорю, они — за войну.
ru.B: Я стою за мир, но стоит мне открыть рот, они выбирают войну.
ru.R: Я хочу мира. Но каждый раз, когда я говорю, они хотят драться.

uk.L: Я — мир; але коли я говорю, вони — за війну.
uk.B: Я стою за мир, та коли відкриваю рот, вони вибирають війну.
uk.R: Я хочу миру. Але щоразу, коли я говорю, вони хочуть битися.

decisions.choice: I am peace: I am wholly for peace
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says simply "I peace": the psalmist's whole self is set on peace, as the enemies are wholly "for war" (109:4 has "I prayer" in the same way).

decisions.choice: peace: whole and good relations
decisions.reason: Peace (shalom) is more than the absence of fighting: it is well-being and right relations between people. The word ties this psalm to the next (122:6-8).

decisions.choice: "chúng" for the enemies
decisions.reason: As in Psalm 1, "chúng" is the usual distancing pronoun for the wicked and for enemies in a psalm.
